html:
In 1520 smallpox reached central Mexico with Spanish soldiers and killed huge numbers of people in the Aztec world, including its ruler. The disease had come from the Old World, and the people of the Americas had never met it before, so they had no immunity.

It arrived with the force of Pánfilo de Narváez, sent from Cuba to arrest Hernán Cortés, who had marched inland without permission. Cortés beat Narváez in May 1520 and took over his men. Spanish accounts say one man in Narváez's force, an enslaved African, was sick with smallpox, and the disease spread from there.

That summer the Aztecs drove the Spanish out of Tenochtitlan, and Moctezuma II died during the fighting. Then the epidemic swept the city. His successor, Cuitláhuac, died of it after ruling for about eighty days. Aztec sources describe bodies covered in sores and whole families dying, with no one left to cook or bury them.

When Cortés came back in 1521 with thousands of local allies, he besieged a city weakened by disease and hunger. Tenochtitlan fell in August 1521, and Spanish rule followed.

Smallpox and later epidemics, such as the cocoliztli of the 1540s, killed a large share of Mexico's people over the following century. It is one of the clearest and most deadly cases of the Columbian Exchange.
